correctness.rationale: PASS: B^j e_0=j^theta e_-j for j>=1 follows by telescoping negative weights and the j=0 initial orbit; lambda on positive indices never enters this fixed vector orbit. For y=(I-B)e_0 and convex coefficients a_0..a_(n-1), the squared norm is sum_(j=0)^n b_j²/R_j with b_j=a_j-a_(j-1), R_0=1, R_j=j^(-2theta), sum b_j=0 and sum(n-j)b_j=1. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz yields 1/[S2-S1²/S0] and equality b_j=R_j(S1-jS0)/D. Since the signed b_j changes sign only once and sums to zero, every proper cumulative a_k is strictly positive, sums to 1, and attains the sharp constrained objective uniquely. Integral comparison gives S2~n^(3-2theta)/(3-2theta) for 1<=theta<3/2 and S2~log n at theta=3/2; the S1²/S0 term is lower-order there, while all moments converge for theta>3/2 to a strictly positive inverse-variance barrier. Independent exact rational coefficient and variational-energy tests reproduce all sample identities but do not prove the asymptotic for every theta.
